84. Shri Krishnadas Ji Varta (Ashtasakha 4)

Now we relate the essence (Bhava) of the Varta of Shri Acharyaji Mahaprabhuji's sevak, Krishnadas Adhikari—one of the Ashtachhap poets whose sacred pads are sung in Seva.

Bhavprakash — In eternal Lila, Krishnadasji is the manifestation of Shri Thakorji's intimate sakha 'Rishabh.' In daytime Lila he is Rishabh Sakha, and in nighttime Nikunj Lila he is Shri Swaminiji's intimate sakhi 'Shri Lalitaji.' Shri Lalitaji manifests in four forms: (1) as the primary Madhya sakhi experiencing the Nikunj-lila of Shri Govardhannathji and Shri Swaminiji; (2) as Rishabh Sakha in the daytime forest lilas; (3) as Damodardas Harsani ('Damala'), ever at the side of Shri Acharyaji; and (4) as Krishnadas Adhikari, who served as chief administrator (Adhikari) at Shri Govardhannathji's temple. Among the eight gates of Shri Girirajji, he is the Mukhiya of the gate at the orchard (bari) opposite Bilchhu (Barsana), through which Shri Govardhannathji goes forth for Raslila.

He was born in Chilotara village in Gujarat to a Kunbi Patel who was the village headman (hakim). At his birth, his father summoned learned Brahmins to foretell the child's traits and lifespan. They declared: "This son will become a great devotee of the Lord; his name will be 'Krishnadas,' and he will not remain at home." Though saddened, his father gave charity and named him Krishnadas. From age five, Krishnadas loved attending Bhagavad-varta; if his parents tried to stop him, he would weep and refuse food, so they let him go freely.

When Krishnadas was twelve or thirteen, a Banjara merchant camped outside the village and earned 14,000 rupees selling goods in Chilotara. That night, thieves colluded with Krishnadas's father to rob the merchant of all 14,000 rupees—his father kept 13,000 and gave 1,000 to the thieves. Discovering this, Krishnadas urged his father to return the stranger's money for his own welfare, but his father beat him. The next morning, when the Banjara wept at the village platform, the father had him driven out of town. Moved with pity, Krishnadas met the Banjara privately and told him: "My father arranged this theft. Go appeal to the King in Rajnagar (Ahmedabad) and summon me as a witness—yet see to it that neither my father nor the thieves are put to death, while you recover your wealth."

The Banjara petitioned the King, who sent fifty soldiers to arrest both father and son. When his father lied, Krishnadas testified truthfully before the King: "As a mortal, he erred—1,000 rupees went to the thieves and 13,000 are with my father. I urged him to return it, but he refused. Please recover the merchant's money without taking his life." The King sent two hundred soldiers, recovered all 14,000 rupees for the Banjara, and stripped the father of his headmanship. Impressed by Krishnadas's truthfulness, the King invited him to stay at court, but Krishnadas declined: "In these times, speaking the truth makes everyone an enemy; I shall become a renunciant."

Taking leave of his father, Krishnadas set out on pilgrimage, bathed at Vishrant Ghat in Mathura, and reached Shri Govardhan, where he heard that a temple had been built for Devdaman (Shri Govardhannathji). Arriving during Rajbhog Aarti, Shri Govardhannathji instantly captivated his heart and told Shri Acharyaji Mahaprabhuji: "This is Krishnadas, separated from Me for so long; that is why I am gazing at him." Shri Acharyaji called out, "Krishnadas! You have come?" Offering Dandavat, Krishnadas begged for refuge. After having him bathe in Rudrakund, Shri Acharyaji granted him Naam and Brahmasambandh before Shri Govardhannathji. Being a daivi jiva, he immediately experienced all eternal Lilas and sang:

Raag Sarang —
"Vallabh patit-uddhaaran jaano |
Sarani let leela darasaavat ta par dharat Govardhanaraano ||1||
Saadhan vritha karat din khovat Shri Vallabh kau roop na jaane |
Jaaki kripa kataaksha saphal phal 'Krishnadas' teenon janam na maane ||2||"
(Know Shri Vallabh as the savior of the fallen! The moment one takes his shelter, he reveals divine Lila and Shri Govardhanrana melts in grace! Those who waste their days in futile practices do not know Shri Vallabh's true form; one blessed by his merciful glance, says Krishnadas, cares nothing for worldly births.)

On the auspicious day of Akshaya Tritiya, Shri Govardhannathji was installed in Purnamal's new temple, and Ramdas Chauhan departed his body for eternal Lila. On Sadu Pande's suggestion, Shri Acharyaji invited twenty to twenty-five Bengalis from Radhakund, built them huts at Rudrakund to perform temple worship, and appointed Krishnadas as Bhetiya (collector of offerings from abroad).

Varta — Prasang 1
Once Krishnadas traveled toward Shri Dwarkaji to collect offerings (bhet) from Vaishnavas. On the return journey he passed through Mirabai's village, where many other-path (anyamargiya) saints and mahants had been waiting ten or twenty days for donations. Krishnadas immediately prepared to depart. When Mirabai urged him to stay, he said: "We stay only with Shri Acharyaji's Vaishnava sevaks, never with followers of other paths." When Mirabai offered eleven gold mohurs as bhet for Shri Nathji, Krishnadas refused even to touch them—"You are not Shri Acharyaji's sevak, so I will not touch your mohurs!"—and walked out.

When his companion Vaishnava asked why he had rejected Shri Govardhannathji's offering, Krishnadas explained: "There is no shortage at Shri Govardhannathji's! Where else could I find so many other-path swamis gathered in one place to humble their pride—seeing that while they waited days for donations, even a Shudra sevak of Shri Acharyaji refused eleven gold mohurs? They now realize the greatness of our Guru! Besides, why should we accept bhet from an anyamargiya?"

Bhavprakash — The Shikshapatra states: 'Tadiyanam mahaddukham vijatiyena sangamah' (For Bhagavadiyas, no sorrow equals association with those of incompatible paths). And Shri Gusainji declares in the Chatushloki:
"Vijatiyajanakirne nijadharmasya gopanam |
Deshe vidhaya satatam stheyamityeva me matih ||1||"
(When amidst people of other paths, one should always guard and conceal one's own dharma.)

Varta — Prasang 2
The Bengali priests served Shri Govardhannathji, yet siphoned off all offerings—even gold and silver platters worth one lakh rupees offered by Shri Gopinathji from his eastern tour—to their gurus in Vrindavan. Moreover, they kept an idol of a Devi hidden in their hair-tuft (chutiya) and placed it beside Shri Nathji during Rajbhog!

Bhavprakash — Avadhutdasji, a Sanadhya Brahmin of Ading, was a beloved sevak of Shri Acharyaji (in Lila, 'Ketini' sakhi of the Kumarika group). Initiated by Shri Acharyaji at Govindkund, he attained an alaukik body and roamed Braj absorbed in mansi seva of Shri Govardhandhar.

One day Shri Govardhannathji instructed Avadhutdasji: "Tell Krishnadas Adhikari to expel these Bengalis; I wish to expand My royal splendor (vaibhav), and I dislike their placing a Devi idol beside Me." Meeting Krishnadas on the road to Mathura, Avadhutdasji relayed the Lord's command. Since Shri Acharyaji had appointed the Bengalis, Krishnadas immediately traveled to Adel to seek Shri Gusainji's permission. Shri Gusainji agreed and gave Krishnadas two letters addressed to Raja Todarmal and Raja Birbal in Agra, affirming Krishnadas as Shri Govardhannathji's Adhikari and requesting their support.

Securing Todarmal and Birbal's backing in Agra, Krishnadas returned to Shri Girirajji and had the Bengalis' huts at Rudrakund set on fire. Hearing the uproar, all the Bengalis abandoned Shri Nathji's Seva and ran down the hill to douse the flames. Seizing the moment, Krishnadas stationed two hundred Brajvasis at the temple and placed Brahmin bhitariya sevaks inside to conduct Seva with care. Standing at the foot of the hill with a staff, he told the Bengalis their service was finished, and when they tried to fight, he drove them away.

The Bengalis complained to Rupa-Sanatana in Mathura, who backed down when Krishnadas boldly arrived in his chariot with fifty armed Brajvasis and challenged them. Next they appealed to the Mathura Hakim and finally to Emperor Akbar in Agra. Todarmal and Birbal explained to Akbar that Shri Govardhannathji belonged to Shri Vitthalnathji (Shri Gusainji) and Krishnadas was His Adhikari. Akbar dismissed the Bengalis' complaint and upheld Krishnadas's authority.

Krishnadas then sent messengers to Adel inviting Shri Gusainji. Arriving at Shri Girirajji, Shri Gusainji draped the Adhikari's shawl (dushala) over Krishnadas before Shri Govardhannathji, established the Adhikari's seat (gadi), and declared: "Krishnadas, you have performed a great service; now exercise full authority over Shri Govardhannathji's house—even if I err, tell me without hesitation!" When the Bengalis later pleaded for a livelihood, Shri Gusainji entrusted them with Shri Gopinathji's sevya Shri Madanmohanji to serve in Vrindavan according to maryada-puja.

Shri Gusainji then appointed Gujarati Sanchora Brahmins as bhitariyas, with Bade Ramdasji as Mukhiya Bhitariya (Bhavprakash: in Lila, 'Manorama' sakhi of Shri Chandravaliji, initiated by Shri Acharyaji at Dwarka, who sang Raag Gauri 'Chali sakhi chali aho Braj penth lagi hai jahaan bikat Hari-ras prem' and spent a month in satsang with Padmanabhdasji in Kannauj). Shri Gusainji greatly expanded Rajseva—appointing tailors, goldsmiths, carpenters, and bhandaris under Krishnadas Adhikari—and Krishnadas's authority and splendor became renowned everywhere.

Varta — Prasang 3
One day Shri Govardhannathji commanded Krishnadas to bring Shyam Kumhar with his mridang to Parasoli after Shayan Aarti for Raslila. (Bhavprakash: in Lila, Shyam Kumhar was Vishakhaji's mridang-playing sakhi 'Rastaragini,' who once spoke proudly when woken to play and was cursed to be born in a potter's home in Mahavan; initiated by Shri Gusainji, he came to serve Shri Nathji.)

On the radiant full-moon night of Chaitra Shukla 15, Krishnadas and Shyam Kumhar reached Parasoli Chandrasarovar, where Shri Govardhandhar and Shri Swaminiji sat surrounded by sakhis. As Shyam Kumhar played the mridang and the Divine Couple danced, Krishnadas sang:

Raag Kedaro —
"Shri Vrishabhaan-nandani naachat Lal Giridharan sang, laag daat urap tirap raas rang raachyau |
Jhap taal milyo raag Kedaro sam suran avaghat-avaghat sugharataan gaan rang raachyo ||1||
Paai sukh surati siddhi bharat kaam vividh riddhi abhinav vadan sam suhaag hulaas rang raachyo |
Banita sat-joothap piya nirakhi thakyo saghan chand balihaari 'Krishnadas' sughar rang raakhyo ||2||"

Delighted, Shri Govardhandhar bestowed the fragrant kund-flower garland from His own neck upon Krishnadas. Overwhelmed with rapture, Krishnadas sang four wondrous Raslila pads in Raag Malav:

Raag Malav —
(1) "Alag laagan urap tirap gati natavat Brajalalana raasen |
Ughatat sabda tatathei tatathei mriganayani ishad haase ||1||
Bhaal chand lajaavat gaavat baandhat madan bhonh paase |
Chalat uraj kati kinkini kundal shramajal-kan sobhit aase ||2||
Nupur kunit kvanit katimekhala katitat kaachhe neel suvaase |
Avaghat taanamaan bandhaane mohit vishva charan nyaase ||3||
Mohanlal Govardhandhaari rijhavat chhel sughar laase |
Apane kanth ki shramajal dalamil maala deti 'Krishnadaase' ||4||"

(2) "Tatathei raasamandal men bane naachat piyake sang preetamapyaari |
Gaavat saras sujaat milavat chapal kutil bhonh aniyaari ||1||
Malav raag alaapati bhaamini leti urap naagar naari |
Pyaari ke sang venu bajaavat sughararaaya Shri Govardhandhaari ||2||
'Krishnadas' Prabhu sobhag seenva sab yuvatin men sukumaari |
Jori adbhut pragatit bhootal kelikalaaras manuhaari ||3||"

(3) "Chand Govind gopi taara gan bane raas men Banavaari |
Mukh prataap ranjit Vrindavan naval yuvatijan sukhakaari ||1||
Kamalanayan kamaneeya manohar manaharani Gokulanaari |
Hastakamal par galit kusumadal nrityamaan preetam pyaari ||2||
Rasamayaraas-rasikani bhaamini atirasaal bane Bihaari |
'Krishnadas' Prabhu rasik shiromani rasikaraaya Girivaradhaari ||3||"

(4) "Sikhavati Harikon murali bajaavat |
Sapta randhra par dharat anguli dal kandh baahoo dhari madhure gaavat ||1||
Sarasabhed gati raag Kaanharo gati bilaasavar nayan nachaavat |
'Krishnadas' bali bali vaibhavaki Giridhar piya pyaari man bhaavat ||2||"

Afterward, Shri Govardhandhar, Shri Swaminiji, and the Brajbhaktas vanished from sight, and Krishnadas and Shyam Kumhar returned to Gopalpur.

Varta — Prasang 4
One day Surdasji teased Krishnadas: "Krishnadas! Every kirtan you compose bears my shadow!" Krishnadas vowed to compose a pad untouched by Surdasji's shadow. Sitting alone for a full prahar, he realized Surdasji had already sung of every lila—Daan, Maan, and the cows! Exhausted, he set down his pen and paper and went to take Mahaprasad.

While he was away, Shri Govardhandhar Himself came and wrote the opening line on the paper describing the 'nechuki' cows (first-calving cows intensely devoted to their calves that no cowherd can easily herd), a subject Surdasji had never sung:

Raag Gauri —
"Aavat ban Kaanha gop-baalak sang nechuki khur-renu chhurit alakaavali |
Bhonh Manmath-chaap vakralochan baan sees sobhit matta mayoor-chandraavali ||1||
Udit uduraaja sundar siromani badan nirakhi phooli naval juvati kumudaavali |
Arun sakuchit adharabimba phal hasat kachhu pragat hot kund dasanaavali ||2||
Shravan kundal bhaal tilak besari naak, kanth kaustubhamani subh trivalaavali |
Ratna haatak khachit, urasi padikani paanti, beech raajati subhra jhalak muktaavali ||3||
Valaya kankan baajooband aajaanubhuj mudrika kar-dal biraajati nakhaavali |
Kunit kar muralika mohit akhil vishva gopika jan-manasi grathit premaavali ||4||
Kati chhudra ghantika jatit heeraamani naabhi ambuj balit bhring romaavali |
Dhaai kabahook chalat bhakt hit jaani piya gand mandit ruchir shramajal-kanaavali ||5||
Peet kausheya paridhaan sundar ang chalat nupur gi sabdaavali |
Hridaya 'Krishnadas' Giridharanalal ki charan-nakh-chandrika harati timiraavali ||6||"

Returning, Krishnadas completed the pad and went laughing to Surdasji. Hearing just the very first line, Surdasji laughed and said: "Krishnadas! The contest is between you and me—not with your Father! What is yours in this? The 'nechuki' cow I hadn't sung was written by the Lord Himself, and the rest of the Shri-ang description is from my thousands of pads!" Krishnadas fell silent. (Bhavprakash explains that Lalita-roop Krishnadas excels in Seva administration while Champakalata-roop Surdas excels in kirtan—each supreme in his own domain.)

Varta — Prasang 5
Once Krishnadas traveled to Agra in his chariot with carts for temple provisions. In the market, a courtesan was teaching her exquisitely beautiful, twelve-year-old daughter to dance and sing khyal-tappa. Captivated by her voice, Krishnadas halted his chariot.

Bhavprakash — In Jalbhed, Shri Acharyaji warns:
"Veshyadisahita matta gayaka gartasanjnitah |
Jalarthameva gartastu nicha ganopajivinah ||"
Why then was Krishnadas, a staunch upholder of maryada, moved by a courtesan's song? Because in eternal Lila the girl was Lalitaji's sakhi 'Bahubhashini.' Once, while carrying ground mishri, she chatted with another sakhi and a drop of saliva fell into it. When she argued back, Lalitaji cursed her to a lowly birth, and she pleaded for Lalitaji to take birth in a Shudra home to rescue her. Thus, inspired by Shri Govardhandhar, Krishnadas came to Agra for her liberation.

Recognizing her as a daivi jiva worthy of Shri Govardhannathji, Krishnadas gave her ten rupees to perform at his haveli that night, rewarded her with a hundred rupees, and invited her to perform before his "Seth" at Shri Govardhan. Traveling to Gopalpur, he had her bathe and wear fresh clothes, and taught her a pad in Raag Purvi:

Raag Purvi —
"Mero man Giridhar chhabi par atakyo |
Lalit tribhangi angan upar chali gayo tahaan hi thathakyo ||1||
Sajal syamaghan neel baran hai phiri chitta anat na bhatakyo |
'Krishnadas' kiyo praan nyochhaavari yah tan jag sir patakyo ||2||"
(My mind is transfixed upon Giridhar's beauty! Drawn to His graceful threefold-curved form, it paused and stayed there forever. Dark blue like a rain-laden cloud, my heart never wanders elsewhere. Krishnadas has sacrificed his very life, casting this mortal body back upon the world!)

At Bhog darshan, Krishnadas brought her up to the temple. As the doors opened, she danced and sang this pad. The instant she sang the final line—"'Krishnadas' kiyo praan nyochhaavari yah tan jag sir patakyo"—her soul departed her body and entered eternal Lila in a divine form! Krishnadas consoled her weeping mother and accompanists with a thousand rupees. (Bhavprakash notes that Brahmasambandh is granted solely by Vallabhkul; hence in eternal Lila, Shri Lalitaji had Shri Swaminiji grant her Brahmasambandh and take her into Seva.)

Varta — Prasang 6
Once a group of Vaishnavas came to Kumbhandasji wishing to hear the principles (riti) of Pushtimarg. Absorbed in rahasya-lila, Kumbhandasji led them to Krishnadas Adhikari as the master of Pushtimarg principles. Welcoming them warmly, Krishnadas sang:

Raag Sarang —
"Giridhar jab apuno kari jaane |
Taakau man bhaktan ki seva bhakt charanaraj sada lubhaane ||1||
Bhaktan men mati bhaktan men gati harijan Hari ek kari maane |
'Krishnadas' man bach kram kari harijan sange Hari ur aane ||2||"

At Kumbhandasji's request, Krishnadas first sang the essence of the Ashtakshar Mantra ('Shri Krishnah Sharanam Mama'):

Raag Sarang —
"Krishna Shri Krishnah sharanam mama uchchare |
Rain din nitya prati sada pal chhin ghadi karat vidhvans jan akhil agh parihare ||1||
Hot Hariroop Brajabhoop bhaave sada agam bhavasindhukon bina saadhan tare |
Rahat nisadivas aanand uramen bhare pushti leela sakal saar ur men dhare ||2||
Rama Aj Siv Sesh Sanakaadi Suk Saarada Vyaas Naarad rate pal mukh na tare |
Lal Giridharanaki mahima atul jagamage saran 'Krishnadas' nigam neti neti kare ||3||"

Next he sang the essence of the Panchakshar Mantra:

Raag Sarang —
"Krishna ye Krishna man maanh gati jaaniye |
Deh indriya praan daaraagaaraadi vitta aatma sakal Shri Krishna ki maaniye ||1||
Krishna mam swami hon daas man vach kram, karta yehi sada jiya aaniye |
'Krishnadasaninaath' Haridasvaryadhar charanaraj Vallabhaadheesh man saaniye ||2||"

Through these two pads, all the Vaishnavas' doubts were dispelled and they departed in deep joy.

Varta — Prasang 7 (and Shri Gusainji's Six-Month Separation)
Krishnadas had deep affection for Gangabai Kshatrani of Mathura (in Lila, a tamasi bhakta in Shrutirupa's group). Having lost nine sons and a daughter, she had been initiated by Shri Acharyaji at Krishnadas's request. To draw her heart to Bhagavaddharma, Krishnadas sent her Mahaprasad and arranged for her to have all of Shri Nathji's darshans.

One day while Shri Gusainji offered Rajbhog to Shri Govardhannathji, Gangabai's gaze fell upon the food. Shri Govardhannathji did not partake of Rajbhog. After concluding Bhog, Shri Gusainji and the sevaks took Mahaprasad and rested. Shri Govardhannathji then came and kicked Bade Ramdas Bhitariya awake, saying: "I am hungry! Gangabai's gaze fell on Rajbhog, so I did not eat."

Ramdasji immediately woke Shri Gusainji, who bathed in the winter cold, went to the temple, and had the bhitariyas quickly cook badi-bhaat, offering both Rajbhog and Shayanbhog together. After Anosar, Shri Gusainji brought down a vessel of badi-bhaat Mahaprasad and shared it with everyone, all praising its extraordinary taste. Standing nearby, Krishnadas remarked sarcastically: "Maharaj! You are both the cook and the eater, so why wouldn't it taste good?" Shri Gusainji replied pointedly: "We are only reaping what you have sown!"

Bhavprakash — The hidden Lila mystery behind this was that earlier that day, Shri Govardhandhar's bhaktoddharak swaroop had gone to Gokul to enjoy badi-bhaat prepared by Shri Giridharji and Shri Shobhabetiji. Hearing of this, Shri Swaminiji also desired badi-bhaat and used Gangabai's gaze to fulfill a prior Lila decree: once Shri Chandravaliji had kept Shri Thakorji away from Lalitaji's nikunj for six months, so Shri Swaminiji declared that Shri Thakorji would remain under Lalitaji's control for six months while Shri Chandravaliji suffered separation. Angered at Lalitaji for inciting this, Shri Chandravaliji cursed her to suffer an untimely death and enter preta-yoni (ghostly state), promising to personally liberate her afterward. Thus, in this alaukik Lila, Shri Gusainji (Shri Chandravaliji) underwent six months of separation with Krishnadas (Shri Lalitaji) as the instrument.

Offended by Shri Gusainji's words, Krishnadas invited Shri Purushottamji (son of Shri Gopinathji, the elder branch's Tiket) to bathe and enter the temple for Seva, while Krishnadas sat at Dandoti Shila and barred Shri Gusainji from climbing the hill. Remembering the eternal Lila, Shri Gusainji offered Dandavat to Shri Nathji's flag and resided in Parasoli for six months (from Paush Shukla 6 to Ashadh Shukla 5) in intense viprayog.

Whenever Krishnadas went down the hill, Shri Govardhannathji would sit at a window (bari) facing Parasoli to give Shri Gusainji darshan; discovering this, Krishnadas had the window bricked up! Yet Mukhiya Bhitariya Bade Ramdasji faithfully brought Shri Nathji's charanodak to Shri Gusainji every day after Rajbhog Aarti, undeterred by Krishnadas's warnings. Shri Gusainji concealed Sanskrit Vigyapti shlokas inside flower garlands sent via Ramdasji, and Shri Nathji wrote replies on betel leaves (paan) using betel juice (peek) and a twig, which Shri Gusainji read, dissolved in water, and drank. One day, overwhelmed with longing, Shri Gusainji wrote:

"Tvaddarshana viheenasya tvadeeyasya tu jeevitam |
Vyarthameva yatha Natha ! durbhagaaya navam vayah ||"
(O Lord! The life of Your devotee deprived of Your darshan is as utterly vain as the blooming youth of an unfortunate woman.)

Shri Nathji replied that just as a cloud rains only at its appointed season, union would come when Krishnadas's time concluded. Shri Gusainji wrote back:

"Ambudasya svabhavo'yam samaye vaari munchati |
Tathapi chaatakah khinno ratatyeva na samshayah ||"
(Though it is the cloud's nature to release rain only in its season, the anguished chataka bird undoubtedly cries out without ceasing!)

On Ashadh Shukla 5, Raja Birbal visited Shri Gokul and learned from Shri Giridharji that Krishnadas had barred Shri Gusainji from darshan for six months. As Faujdar of Mathura, Birbal dispatched five hundred men to arrest Krishnadas and imprison him in Mathura, sending word to Shri Giridharji. At dawn on Ashadh Shukla 6, Shri Giridharji rode to Parasoli to invite Shri Gusainji back to the temple. Hearing that Krishnadas had been imprisoned, Shri Gusainji cried out in distress: "Alas! Such suffering for Shri Acharyaji Mahaprabhuji's beloved Bhagavadiya! I shall not take food until Krishnadas returns!"

Shri Giridharji immediately rode to Mathura, secured Krishnadas's release from an astonished Birbal, and brought him to Parasoli. Seeing Krishnadas arrive, Shri Gusainji rose respectfully as for Shri Govardhannathji's Adhikari. Utterly humbled, Krishnadas fell at his feet and sang:

Raag Sarang —
"Taahi kon sir naaniye jo Shri Vallabhasut padaraj rati hoi |
Keeje kaha aan oonche pad tinason kaha sagaai moi ||1||
Jaake manamen ugra bharam hai Shri Vitthal Shri Giridhar doi |
Taakau sang visham vish hoo te bhoole chatur karo jini koi ||2||
Saaraasaar vichaar mato kari shruti-vach godhan liyo nichoi |
Tahaan navaneet pragat Purushottam sahajai goras liyo hai biloi ||3||
Ugra prataap dekhi apane chakshu asmasaar jyon bhide na toya |
'Krishnadas' sur ten asur bhae asur ten sur bhae charanan chhoya ||4||"

Begging forgiveness, Krishnadas escorted Shri Gusainji up to the temple. On Ashadh Shukla 6, Shri Gusainji offered kasumal kulah-pichhora, completed Seva through Shayan, and once again draped the Adhikari's dushala upon Krishnadas before Shri Nathji. Krishnadas sang:

Raag Kanharo —
"Param kripaal Shri Vallabhanandan karat kripa nij haath de maathai |
Je jan sarani aae anusar hi gahi sompat Shri Govardhannathai ||1||
Param udaar chatur chintaamani raakhat bhavadhaara ten saathai |
Bhaji 'Krishnadas' kaaj sab sarahi jo jaanen Shri Vitthalanaathai ||2||"

When Krishnadas again begged forgiveness for his offense, Shri Gusainji said: "Shri Nathji will forgive your offense."

Varta — Prasang 8 (Visit to Vrindavan and High Fever)
Once Krishnadas visited Shri Gusainji in Shri Gokul, where he was warmly welcomed with Shri Navanitpriyaji's Mahaprasad and a fine bed. Next morning he asked to visit Vrindavan; Shri Gusainji cautioned him: "Go if you wish, but you will suffer." Unable to resist, Krishnadas rode alone to Vrindavan. At midday while meeting local saints, he was struck by intense fever and parched thirst. Refusing water from anyone except a Vallabhi Vaishnava of Gokul, the saints taunted him that only a Gokul sweeper (bhangi) married there was present. Krishnadas declared: "That Gokul sweeper is supreme! Ask him to bathe in the Yamuna and bring water in a new earthen pot."

Instead, the sweeper ran to Gokul Ghat and informed Shri Gusainji from behind a cloth screen. Instantly taking a water jhari, Shri Gusainji mounted a horse, rode to Vrindavan, lifted Krishnadas on his chariot, and gave him water—instantly curing his fever! Bowing in gratitude, Krishnadas sang:

Raag Kanharo —
"Shri Vitthalaju ke charanani ki bali |
Hamase patit uddhaaran param kripaal aapu aae chali ||1||
Ujval arun daya rang ranjit nakhachandra virahatam nirdali |
Sevat sukhakar sobha paavat bhakt mudit lalit pad anguli ||2||
Atisai mridul sugandh su seetal parasat trividh taap daarat mali |
Kahe 'Krishnadas' baar ek sudhi kari tero kaha karego ripu kali ||3||"

Confessing his folly, Krishnadas returned with Shri Gusainji to Shri Govardhan and sang at Shayan Aarti:

Raag Kanharo —
"Aaju kau din dhani dhaniri maai nainan dekhe Nand nandan |
Param udaar manohar moorati taap harat lakhi, poojat chandan ||1||
Navalaraaya Shri Govardhandhaari roop raasi yuvati man phandan |
Dhvaja vajraankus jav biraajat 'Krishnadas' keeno pad vandan ||2||"

Varta — Prasang 9 (The Well)
A Vaishnava entrusted three hundred rupees to Krishnadas to build a well in the garden near Puchhari and returned home. Krishnadas buried one hundred rupees in an earthen pot (kulhara) beneath a mango tree in the garden and spent two hundred rupees constructing the well, reserving the hundred for its parapet (mohado). One day after Utthapan darshan, leaning on his wooden staff (asa) to inspect the well, the staff slipped and Krishnadas fell in. Men descended with ropes and baskets to search, yet not even his body was found.

When news reached Shri Gusainji, Bade Ramdasji remarked, "Tamasanaam adhogatih" (tamasi souls go downward). Shri Gusainji immediately rebuked him: "Ramdasji, do not say that! Krishnadas was Shri Acharyaji Mahaprabhuji's beloved Vaishnava—this is divine Lila!" (Bhavprakash: Shri Gusainji knew the Lila curse had taken effect; Krishnadas had entered preta-yoni in his very body and sat atop a peepal tree near Puchhari.)

Varta — Prasang 10 (The New Adhikari and Liberation at Dhruvaghat)
Shri Gusainji pondered whom to appoint as the next Adhikari without causing a soul's spiritual downfall. (Bhavprakash cites Shri Subodhiniji: authority breeds pride, which is why Shrimad Bhagavatam bore full fruit not for Brahma, Narada, or Vyasa, but for totally renounced Shukadeva and Parikshit.) Asking Shri Govardhannathji after Shayan Aarti, the Lord advised: "Hold out the Adhikari's dushala before all and say whoever wishes to serve may wear it; whoever is destined to fall will step forward himself." Next day at Rajbhog Aarti, a Kshatriya stepped forward first and received the dushala.

Some days later, Shri Govardhannathji's buffalo went missing. Searching near Puchhari, Gopinathdas Gwal and other cowherds saw Shri Govardhannathji playing with sakhas beneath a peepal tree—while Krishnadas Adhikari sat atop the tree as a preta! Greeting Gopinathdas with "Jai Shri Krishna," Krishnadas pleaded: "Brother, convey my supplication to Shri Gusainji! This state is the result of my offense against him. Because he said 'Shri Nathji will forgive you,' Shri Govardhandhar gives me darshan, yet only Shri Gusainji can free me from preta-yoni! Also tell him that one hundred rupees are buried in an earthen pot under the mango tree toward Bilchhu to finish the well's parapet—and Shri Nathji's missing buffalo is grazing in that thicket."

Hearing this from Gopinathdas, Shri Gusainji was deeply moved. He immediately had the hundred rupees dug up and given to the new Adhikari to complete Krishnadas's well, and rode that very night to Mathura. At dawn, Shri Gusainji personally performed Krishnadas's kriya-karma and shraddha at Dhruvaghat, freeing him from preta-yoni and granting him a divine form to enter eternal Lila as Mukhiya of the gate opposite Bilchhu. (Bhavprakash explains that while Shri Gusainji's mere wish sufficed, he performed the Dhruvaghat shraddha to uphold worldly maryada and glorify Dhruvaghat.)

Thus, Krishnadasji's Varta is supremely transcendental. Shri Gusainji himself praised him, saying no one else could compose such wondrous Raslila kirtans, render such Seva, or exercise such authority for Shri Nathji. Such was Krishnadas Adhikari, a most blessed Bhagavadiya of Shri Acharyaji Mahaprabhuji—his Varta is beyond words; how far can it be told?

|| Varta 84 ||
Thus concludes the Chaurasi Vaishnavan Ki Varta as revealed by Shri Gokulnathji, with its Bhavprakash expounded by Shri Harirayji.

Raag Bihag —
"Dridh in charanan kero bharoso, dridh || Refrain ||
Shri Vallabh nakhachandra chhata bin sab jagamaanjh andhero ||1||
Saadhan aur nahin ya kali men jaason hot nivero |
'Soor' kaha kahe dvividh aandharo bina molako chero ||2||"
(Firm, utterly firm is my trust in these lotus feet! Without the moon-like radiance of Shri Vallabh's toenails, the entire world is plunged in darkness. In this age of Kali there is no other means of deliverance. What more can Sur—doubly blind and a servant bought without price—say?)
